items.text: Rams WR Puka Nacua suffered what is believed to be a minor calf injury after leaving Thursday practice early; listed limited.
items.why: Exited practice with calf; sources indicate minor but monitor Friday/Saturday reports closely given Adams absence.
items.implication: If active, massive target share; if limited/out, heavy TE reliance and Atwell/Whittington upside.
items.opportunity: 25+ targets per game potential if plays (post-Adams/Ferguson delay).

items.text: Bears TE Cole Kmet suffered a non-contact knee injury late in the win over the Patriots, was carted off, ruled out, and will undergo further tests; coach Ben Johnson said 'I don’t think it looked very good.'
items.why: Non-contact knee injury with poor visual and coach comments; tests pending but already ruled out for immediate impact.
items.implication: Significant loss for Bears TE room and short-yardage/red-zone; opens route opportunities in 11/12 personnel.
items.opportunity: Increased snaps/routes for remaining TEs and WRs in reduced multi-TE sets.

items.text: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) DNP Thursday after DNP Wednesday; looks likely to miss Week 7 vs SEA unless major Friday progress. Xavier Worthy in line for elevated role.
items.why: Consecutive DNPs post-bye; lingering hamstring + new knee designation.
items.implication: Sit Rice; elevate Worthy as flex/WR3 with target bump.
items.opportunity: Worthy snap/route/target share increase; Kelce also benefits.

items.text: Multiple teams would be open to a potential trade for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor; unclear if Colts ready to unload before deadline.
items.why: Source confirmation of multi-team interest amid Colts evaluation of roster moves.
items.implication: ROS uncertainty for JT value; potential landing spot boost or Indy handcuff surge if moved.
items.opportunity: Monitor depth chart and new team role if traded.

items.text: Josh Jacobs allowed in team meetings, lifting, medical treatments and non-football activities at facility. MarShawn Lloyd (49th EPA/rush of 54) and Kaleb Johnson (53rd) have been quite bad (OL mess too). Discussed long-term Jacobs outlook on ROS Top-150.
items.why: Non-football participation signals recovery path; backups inefficient on EPA.
items.implication: Jacobs closer to return; do not overvalue Lloyd/Johnson as pure handcuffs long-term.
items.opportunity: Jacobs reclaims lead role soon; monitor practice upgrades.

items.text: Saquon Barkley 'in line' to play vs DAL (RB15 rank) after efficient full games; loves Jaylen Warren @ NO, Chuba Hubbard vs TB, Bucky Irving @ CAR for big workloads in friendly matchups.
items.why: Barkley efficiency + DAL soft vs RBs; others volume + matchup.
items.implication: Start Saquon if active; strong RB2/flex plays for the loves.
items.opportunity: Carries, snaps, goal-line in positive scripts.

items.text: Terrance Ferguson (eligible off IR next week) not expected ready soon per Schefter source ('will take some time'); Rams' only answer now is 25 Puka Nacua targets per game post-Adams.
items.why: Ferguson delay removes primary Adams replacement; Puka already high-volume and efficiency king.
items.implication: Elite WR1 floor/ceiling if healthy; stash Ferguson longer-term.
items.opportunity: Extreme target monopoly and red-zone work.

items.text: Loves A.J. Brown @ CHI (WR10): 33% target share, 97% routes in Week 6 despite 3 catches/3 drops/27 yards on 10 targets; buying the volume and Bears matchup.
items.why: Elite usage metrics despite inefficiency; strong matchup vs Bears defense allowing yardage.
items.opportunity: High target share and route participation.

items.text: Loves DeVonta Smith vs DAL (WR11) for elite volume and Tucker Kraft @ DET (TE6) vs Lions secondary that has been a gift to opposing pass catchers.
items.why: Smith volume + Kraft matchup vs soft Lions pass D (high completion % deep, fantasy buffet).
items.implication: Strong starts; Kraft streaming TE upside.

items.text: Hates Rome Odunze vs NE, Josh Downs @ MIN, Travis Kelce @ SEA, Josh Jacobs @ DET, and Cam Skattebo @ HOU due to tough matchups, role/target-share issues, workload questions post-layoff, and brutal spots.
items.why: Nasty defenses, low target share on low-scoring offense, Jacobs workload uncertainty, Skattebo tough matchup.
items.implication: Sit or fade these in Week 7 lineups.
items.conflict: Jacobs facility progress may mitigate some hate.

items.text: Thorman Snaps & Pace: Up in pace TB @ CAR (and GB @ DET, LAR @ LV high volume/explosives); slow slogs MIA @ NYJ, SF @ ATL, IND @ MIN. Bears D fraudulent notes and high-volume environments favored.
items.why: Neutral pace, PROE, combined snaps, and explosive rates identify volume environments vs clock-killers.
items.implication: Prioritize skill players in up-pace games (TB/CAR, DET/GB, LAR/LV); avoid or lower expectations in slogs.
items.opportunity: Higher snap counts, plays, and fantasy points in identified high-pace matchups.

items.text: Yards per target when throwing to Justin Jefferson: Mullens 10.8, Cousins 10.5, Darnold 10.0, Wentz 9.9, JJ McCarthy 5.7. Tough to ignore despite scheme/coach/small sample caveats; Giants plan to start McCarthy vs HOU.
items.why: Dramatically lower efficiency with McCarthy; new Giants start adds uncertainty.
items.implication: Temper Jefferson expectations/ROS if McCarthy under center long-term; monitor chemistry.
items.opportunity: Still high volume but lower YAC/YPT ceiling.

items.text: Bears have Week 10 bye then close fantasy season vs Saints (27th YPP allowed), Lions (24th), Jags (26th), Dolphins (21st), Bills (25th), Packers (3rd), Lions (24th). Soft remaining slate after early weather/backup QB issues.
items.why: Favorable defensive matchups post-bye for volume and efficiency.
items.implication: Buy low on Bears skill players for ROS; elevated QB/WR/RB floors.
items.opportunity: Increased scoring environment and target/carry upside.
